cases.name: Santa Fe Independent School District v. Doe

components.decision: The Court invalidated the school’s student-led, student-selected prayer policy before football games.
components.scope: The school policy and public-address setting mattered; this was not a ban on students praying privately.
components.survey_fit: The question names student-led prayer, school-sponsored events, the public-address system and football games. This is closer than graduation prayer, but omits Santa Fe’s election procedure and full school policy; it remains contextual rather than ruling approval.

cases.name: Good News Club v. Milford Central School

components.issue: Religious viewpoint in an after-school forum
components.decision: Excluding the club because of its religious viewpoint violated the Free Speech Clause.
components.scope: Access for a private club in a limited public forum, not school-led religious instruction.
components.locator: Syllabus, holdings 1–2; Thomas opinion, Parts II–IV.
components.survey_fit: Pew separately asks about student religious groups and religious groups generally; Gallup provides another student-group question. General-group wording avoids assuming a student-led club, but none specifies adult leadership, elementary-age children, parental permission or the full forum rules. Not objecting to access is not the same as requiring it constitutionally.
